title: Can Pakistan triple its incomes by 2050?
credits: Photos: Shujaat Muzaffar, Muhammad Amir, Hassan Anwer / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Could the average Pakistani be three times richer by twenty fifty? The World Bank says yes, but only with faster reforms.
Its new Pakistan Development Update is titled Attaining Escape Velocity.
It says Pakistan's economy grew three point seven percent in the last fiscal year, up from three point two percent the year before.
The government also posted a record primary budget surplus, of two point nine percent of GDP.
But growth per person is stuck at about one point six percent a year, too slow to change most people's lives.
If Pakistan's policies and institutions matched those of an average middle-income country, growth could reach six to seven percent a year.
That would triple incomes by twenty fifty, to the level Vietnam has today.
The World Bank wants a better business environment, a tax overhaul, a smaller role for the state, and more access to finance.
Its country director, Bolormaa Amgaabazar, says reforms to drive faster growth are now urgently needed.
The IMF adds a warning: because of the Iran war, it expects the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan region to shrink by one point three percent this year.
It describes the outlook as clouded by exceptionally high uncertainty, with oil prices the biggest risk.
